mission shall be twenty-eight percent (28%) of Ceded Premiums (the \"Minimum Ceding Commission\").

The sliding scale commission table is set forth in further detail in Schedule B attached hereto.

**7.3 Adjustment Timing.** The sliding scale adjustment shall be calculated annually based on the development of the Treaty Year Loss Ratio. The initial sliding scale adjustment shall be made at the first annual settlement following the expiration of the Treaty Period (i.e., the adjustment as of December 31, 2026, based on losses developed as of that date). Subsequent adjustments shall be made annually thereafter until all Ceded Losses on Subject Business are finally settled and paid, or until this Treaty is commuted pursuant to Article XVII. Each annual adjustment shall be based on the cumulative Treaty Year Loss Ratio calculated as of the most recent calendar year-end.

**7.4 True-Up.** Following each annual sliding scale adjustment, the difference between the aggregate provisional commission previously paid and the adjusted commission determined under the sliding scale (the \"True-Up Amount\") shall be calculated. If the adjusted commission exceeds the aggregate provisional commission previously paid, the Reinsurer shall pay the excess to the Company. If the aggregate provisional commission previously paid exceeds the adjusted commission, the Company shall reimburse the excess to the Reinsurer. The True-Up Amount shall be settled in the next quarterly account following the date of the annual adjustment calculation.

**7.5 No Floor on Loss Ratio for Commission Purposes.** For the avoidance of doubt, the Loss Ratio used to calculate the sliding scale ceding commission shall be the actual cumulative Loss Ratio for the Treaty Year without any floor, cap, or adjustment, and shall include all Ceded Losses (including ALAE) up to and including any losses subject to the Aggregate Limit set forth in Article VI.

**7.6 Example.** By way of illustration only, if the Treaty Year Loss Ratio as of a given annual adjustment date is 62.30%, the Ceding Commission would be calculated as follows:

> Ceding Commission = 38.00% − \[(62.30% − 55.00%) × 0.40\] Ceding Commission = 38.00% − \[7.30 × 0.40\] Ceding Commission = 38.00% − 2.92% Ceding Commission = 35.08%

**[ARTICLE VIII --- PROFIT COMMISSION]{.underline}**

**8.1 Profit Commission.** In addition to the Ceding Commission payable under Article VII, the Reinsurer shall pay the Company a profit commission equal to fifteen percent (15%) of Net Treaty Profit, if any, for each Treaty Year.

**8.2 Calculation of Net Treaty Profit.** For purposes of this Article VIII, \"Net Treaty Profit\" shall be calculated as follows:

> \(a\) Start with Ceded Premiums for the Treaty Year;
>
> \(b\) Subtract Ceded Losses (including ALAE) for the Treaty Year;
>
> \(c\) Subtract the Ceding Commission (as adjusted pursuant to the sliding scale under Article VII) for the Treaty Year;
>
> \(d\) Subtract an overhead and margin allowance equal to five percent (5%) of Ceded Premiums for the Treaty Year (the \"Overhead Allowance\");
>
> \(e\) The result, if positive, is the Net Treaty Profit for the Treaty Year.

Expressed as a formula:

> Net Treaty Profit = Ceded Premiums − Ceded Losses (incl. ALAE) − Ceding Commission − (5% × Ceded Premiums)

If the result of the foregoing calculation is zero or negative, there shall be no Net Treaty Profit for the Treaty Year, and no profit commission shall be payable.

**8.3 Deficit Carryforward.** If the Net Treaty Profit calculation results in a negative amount (a \"Deficit\") in any Treaty Year or annual recalculation period, such Deficit shall carry forward and must be recovered in full before any profit commission becomes payable to the Company in subsequent annual recalculation periods. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Deficits shall carry forward for a maximum of two (2) consecutive annual recalculation periods, after which any remaining Deficit shall extinguish and the profit commission calculation shall reset as if no Deficit existed.

**8.4 Timing of Calculation.** The initial profit commission calculation shall be made twenty-four (24) months after the Expiration Date (i.e., as of December 31, 2027, based on losses developed through that date). Subsequent profit commission recalculations shall be made annually thereafter, on each anniversary of the initial calculation date, until all Ceded Losses are finally settled and paid, or until this Treaty is commuted pursuant to Article XVII. Each profit commission recalculation shall be based on cumulative data for the Treaty Year.

**8.5 Payment.** Any profit commission determined to be payable to the Company shall be settled in the next quarterly account following the applicable annual profit commission calculation.

**8.6 Illustration.** An illustrative example of the profit commission calculation is set forth in Schedule C attached hereto. The example is provided for illustration purposes only and shall not constitute a guarantee or prediction of actual results.

**[ARTICLE IX --- ACCOUNTS AND SETTLEMENTS]{.underline}**

**9.1 Quarterly Accounts.** The Company shall prepare and submit to the Reinsurer quarterly accounts of all transactions under this Treaty within forty-five (45) days following the end of each calendar quarter (i.e., within forty-five (45) days following March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31 of each year). The quarterly accounts shall continue to be submitted for so long as there are outstanding obligations under this Treaty, including during the run-off period following the Expiration Date.

**9.2 Contents of Quarterly Accounts.** Each quarterly account shall include the following:

> \(a\) **Premium Bordereau:** A detailed listing of all Subject Business policies incepting, renewing, or canceling during the applicable quarter, including the policy number, named insured, effective date, policy limits, gross premium, net premium, and ceded premium for each policy;
>
> \(b\) **Loss Bordereau:** A detailed listing of all claims under Subject Business, including the claim number, date of loss, date of report, nature of claim, paid losses, case reserves, incurred losses, and ALAE for each claim, together with the Reinsurer\'s ceded share of each item;
>
> \(c\) **Ceding Commission Statement:** A statement of the ceding commission due for the applicable quarter, calculated at the Provisional Ceding Commission rate (or the adjusted rate following any annual sliding scale adjustment);
>
> \(d\) **Net Balance:** A summary showing the net balance due from or to each Party for the applicable quarter, calculated as Ceded Premiums less Ceded Losses paid less Ceding Commission.

**9.3 Books and Records Conclusive.** The Company\'s books and records shall be conclusive as to all matters set forth in the quarterly accounts, absent manifest error. If the Reinsurer identifies a manifest error in any quarterly account, the Reinsurer shall notify the Company in writing within ninety (90) days of receipt of such account, and the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to resolve the error. Any correction resulting from the resolution of a manifest error shall be reflected in the next quarterly account following resolution.

**9.4 Settlement of Net Balances.** Net balances shown in the quarterly accounts shall be remitted by the owing Party within forty-five (45) days of the end of the applicable calendar quarter. For the avoidance of doubt, the forty-five (45) day settlement period runs concurrently with the forty-five (45) day period for submission of the quarterly account. Accordingly, the net balance for any quarter shall be due and payable no later than forty-five (45) days after the end of such quarter.

**9.5 Late Payment Interest.** Any amount due from either Party under this Treaty that is not paid when due shall bear interest at the rate of the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (\"SOFR\") as published by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York (or any successor rate) on the date such payment becomes due, plus two and one-half percent (2.50%) per annum, compounded quarterly, from the due date until the date of actual payment. The accrual of late payment interest shall not be deemed a waiver of any other rights or remedies available to the non-defaulting Party.

**9.6 Currency.** All amounts under this Treaty, including all premiums, losses, commissions, and other payments, shall be in United States Dollars.

**9.7 Netting.** The Parties agree that all amounts due under this Treaty may be netted against each other in each quarterly account, such that only a single net payment is required from the owing Party for each quarter. The right of netting under this Section 9.7 is without prejudice to the broader offset rights set forth in Article XIII.

**[ARTICLE X --- REPORTS AND RECORDS]{.underline}**

**10.1 Maintenance of Records.** The Company shall maintain complete and accurate books, records, and accounts of all transactions under this Treaty in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles (\"GAAP\") and statutory accounting principles (\"SAP\") as applicable to the Company\'s financial reporting obligations. Such books, records, and accounts shall include, without limitation, policy records, premium records, claims files, loss reserve records, and all supporting documentation.

**10.2 Right of Inspection and Audit.** The Reinsurer, acting through its authorized officers, employees, or appointed representatives (including independent auditors or actuaries), shall have the right, upon not less than thirty (30) days\' prior written notice, to inspect and audit the books, records, and accounts of the Company relating to Subject Business during normal business hours at the Company\'s offices. Such inspections and audits shall be conducted at the Reinsurer\'s sole cost and expense. The Company shall make its relevant personnel reasonably available for interviews and inquiries during any such inspection or audit. The Reinsurer\'s right of inspection and audit shall survive the expiration or termination of this Treaty and shall continue for so long as the Reinsurer has any outstanding obligations hereunder.

**10.3 Additional Reports.** The Company shall furnish to the Reinsurer such additional reports, data, analyses, and information relating to Subject Business as the Reinsurer may reasonably request from time to time, including without limitation actuarial reports, underwriting summaries, large loss reports, and financial statements. The Company shall respond to such requests within a reasonable time, taking into account the nature and complexity of the information requested.

**10.4 Cooperation.** Each Party shall cooperate fully with the other in connection with any audit, inspection, or information request under this Article X. The Parties acknowledge that the timely exchange of accurate information is essential to the proper administration of this Treaty.

**[ARTICLE XI --- CLAIMS COOPERATION, REPORTING, AND SETTLEMENT AUTHORITY]{.underline}**

**11.1 Claims Handling.** The Company shall investigate, adjust, defend, and settle all claims arising under Subject Business in accordance with the Company\'s customary claims handling practices and procedures. The Company shall handle all such claims with the same degree of care and diligence as if no reinsurance existed under this Treaty.

**11.2 Individual Claim Reporting.** The Company shall give written notice to the Reinsurer of any individual claim under Subject Business that equals or exceeds Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000) in incurred losses (defined as the sum of paid losses plus outstanding case reserves, including ALAE) within sixty (60) days of such claim first reaching or exceeding the Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollar (\$250,000) threshold. The notice shall include the claim number, the date of loss, the date of report to the Company, the identity of the claimant and the insured, a description of the claim, the amounts paid and reserved, and an assessment of the Company\'s exposure. The Company shall provide the Reinsurer with updated information regarding each such reported claim on a quarterly basis as part of the loss bordereau required under Article IX, or more frequently if there is a material development in the claim.

**11.3 Quarterly Loss Reporting.** In addition to the individual claim reporting required by Section 11.2, the Company shall provide the quarterly loss bordereau reports as set forth in Article IX, which shall include information on all claims under Subject Business regardless of amount.

**11.4 Settlement Authority / Consent to Settle.** The Company shall have full authority to investigate, adjust, and settle claims under Subject Business without the Reinsurer\'s consent where the total incurred losses (paid plus reserves, including ALAE) on such claim are less than Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000). For any individual claim under Subject Business where total incurred losses equal or exceed Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000), the Company shall obtain the Reinsurer\'s prior written consent before entering into any settlement, compromise, or consent judgment. The Reinsurer shall respond to any request for settlement consent within a reasonable time following the Company\'s submission of sufficient information to enable the Reinsurer to evaluate the proposed settlement. The Company shall provide to the Reinsurer all relevant information in its possession regarding the claim, including the claim file, coverage analysis, liability analysis, damages assessment, and the terms of the proposed settlement.

**11.5 Right to Associate.** The Reinsurer shall have the right to associate at its own expense in the defense and control of any claim under Subject Business where total incurred losses (paid plus reserves, including ALAE) equal or exceed Seven Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$750,000). The Reinsurer shall exercise its right to associate by giving written notice to the Company. Upon exercise of such right, the Company shall cooperate fully with the Reinsurer in the conduct of the defense of such claim, including providing access to all relevant claim files, correspondence, and documentation. The Reinsurer\'s right to associate shall include the right to appoint counsel of its choice to participate in the defense of such claim, and the Company shall not unreasonably refuse such appointment. Notwithstanding the Reinsurer\'s right to associate, the Company shall retain primary responsibility for the management and conduct of the defense of all claims, subject to the Reinsurer\'s consent rights under Section 11.4. The Reinsurer\'s decision not to exercise its right to associate shall not waive or otherwise affect any of the Reinsurer\'s rights under this Treaty.

**11.6 No Voluntary Payments.** The Company shall not make any voluntary payments, extra-contractual obligations payments, or ex gratia payments on behalf of the Reinsurer without the Reinsurer\'s prior written consent. Any such payment made without the Reinsurer\'s consent shall not be included in Ceded Losses.

**11.7 Extra-Contractual Obligations.** This Treaty does not cover extra-contractual obligations (\"ECO\"), including bad faith claims, punitive damages, or other liabilities arising from the Company\'s handling of claims, unless the Reinsurer provides its prior written consent to include such obligations within the scope of Ceded Losses.

**11.8 Claims Cooperation.** Each Party shall cooperate fully with the other in connection with the investigation, adjustment, defense, and settlement of claims under Subject Business. The Parties shall share information relevant to claims on a timely basis and shall consult with each other regarding claims strategy and significant developments in material claims.

**[ARTICLE XII --- SALVAGE AND SUBROGATION]{.underline}**

**12.1 Reinsurer\'s Share.** The Reinsurer\'s share of any salvage, subrogation, or other recovery (including any recovery from third parties, co-defendants, or other insurers) obtained by the Company with respect to Ceded Losses shall be in proportion to the Quota Share Percentage (thirty percent (30%)). All such recoveries shall be credited to the Reinsurer in the quarterly accounts in which they are received by the Company.

**12.2 Net of Recovery Costs.** Salvage, subrogation, and other recoveries shall be credited to the Reinsurer net of the Company\'s reasonable costs of recovery, including legal fees, collection costs, and other expenses directly attributable to the recovery effort. The Reinsurer\'s share of recovery costs shall also be in proportion to the Quota Share Percentage.

**12.3 Duty to Pursue.** The Company shall pursue salvage, subrogation, and other recoveries in a commercially reasonable manner consistent with its customary practices. The Company shall not waive, release, or compromise any right of salvage or subrogation with respect to Ceded Losses without the Reinsurer\'s prior written consent where the potential recovery exceeds Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000). The Company shall keep the Reinsurer informed of significant salvage and subrogation matters and shall consult with the Reinsurer regarding the pursuit and settlement of material recovery claims.

**[ARTICLE XIII --- OFFSET]{.underline}**

**13.1 Right of Offset.** Each Party shall have the right to offset any balance or amounts due from one Party to the other under this Treaty against any balance or amounts due under any other reinsurance agreement between the Parties, whether such other agreement was entered into before, during, or after the term of this Treaty, and whether such amounts are due on account of premiums, losses, commissions, or other obligations. The right of offset may be exercised at any time and shall not require the consent or agreement of the other Party.

**13.2 Survival.** The right of offset set forth in this Article XIII shall survive the termination, expiration, or commutation of this Treaty and shall continue until all obligations between the Parties under all reinsurance agreements are fully discharged.

**13.3 Notice.** Any Party exercising its right of offset shall provide written notice to the other Party specifying the amounts offset and the agreements to which such amounts relate, within thirty (30) days of exercising such right.

**[ARTICLE XIV --- INSOLVENCY]{.underline}**

**14.1 Payment Obligation.** In the event of the insolvency of the Company, the Reinsurer\'s obligations under this Treaty shall be payable to the Company or its successors, without diminution because of the insolvency of the Company, and without requirement that the Company or its successors first pay the loss for which the reinsurance is due. The reinsurance shall be payable by the Reinsurer on the basis of the liability of the Company under the policies of insurance reinsured hereunder, without diminution because of the insolvency of the Company. It is understood and agreed that in the event of the insolvency of the Company, the Reinsurer\'s obligation to pay Ceded Losses shall not be contingent upon the Company\'s or its successors\' prior payment to policyholders or claimants.

**14.2 Filing of Claims.** All claims against the Reinsurer arising under this Treaty in the event of the insolvency of the Company shall be filed with the liquidator, receiver, or statutory successor of the Company on a timely basis. The Reinsurer shall cooperate with the liquidator, receiver, or statutory successor in the administration of claims under this Treaty.

**14.3 Right to Investigate and Defend.** The Reinsurer shall have the right to investigate any claim filed against it in connection with the insolvency of the Company and to interpose, at its own expense, in any proceeding where such claim is to be adjudicated, any defenses that it may deem available to the Company or its estate, or any defenses that it may deem available to the Reinsurer. The exercise of such right shall not be deemed an admission of liability by the Reinsurer.

**14.4 Basis of Payment.** Any payment made by the Reinsurer in connection with the insolvency of the Company shall be made to the Company or its successors on the basis of the liability of the Company under the policy or policies of insurance reinsured hereunder, without diminution because of the insolvency. The Reinsurer shall not be liable for any penalties, fines, or additional amounts assessed against the Company or its estate in connection with the insolvency proceedings, except to the extent such amounts constitute Ceded Losses as defined herein.

**14.5 Applicable Law.** This Article XIV shall be interpreted and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois, including without limitation the Illinois Insurance Code (215 ILCS 5/1 et seq.) and the regulations promulgated thereunder, notwithstanding the choice of law provision in Article XV.

**[ARTICLE XV --- ARBITRATION]{.underline}**

**15.1 Dispute Resolution.** Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Treaty, including its formation, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination (a \"Dispute\"), that cannot be resolved by good faith negotiation between the senior management of the Parties within sixty (60) days of written notice from one Party to the other specifying the nature of the Dispute, shall be submitted to and finally resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with this Article XV.

**15.2 Seat of Arbitration.** The seat (legal place) of arbitration shall be Hamilton, Bermuda.

**15.3 Procedural Law.** The arbitration shall be conducted in accordance with the procedural rules and requirements of the Bermuda Arbitration Act 1986, as amended from time to time, except to the extent such rules are modified by the provisions of this Article XV.

w.** This Treaty shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of Bermuda, without regard to any conflict-of-laws principles that would result in the application of the laws of another jurisdiction; provided, however, that Article XIV (Insolvency) shall be interpreted and applied in accordance with the laws of the State of Illinois, as set forth in Section 14.5.

**15.5 Arbitration Panel.** The arbitration shall be conducted by a panel of three (3) arbitrators, appointed as follows:

> \(a\) Within thirty (30) days of the delivery of a demand for arbitration by either Party, the demanding Party shall appoint one (1) arbitrator and shall notify the other Party of such appointment;
>
> \(b\) Within thirty (30) days of receipt of such notification, the responding Party shall appoint one (1) arbitrator and shall notify the demanding Party of such appointment;
>
> \(c\) The two (2) party-appointed arbitrators shall, within thirty (30) days of the appointment of the second arbitrator, select a third arbitrator to serve as the umpire of the panel;
>
> \(d\) If either Party fails to appoint an arbitrator within the time specified above, the other Party may apply to the President of the Bermuda International Conciliation and Arbitration (\"BICA\") to make the appointment on behalf of the defaulting Party;
>
> \(e\) If the two party-appointed arbitrators fail to agree upon the selection of the umpire within the time specified above, either Party may apply to the President of BICA to appoint the umpire.

**15.6 Qualifications.** All arbitrators, including the umpire, shall be current or former officers, directors, or senior executives of insurance or reinsurance companies and shall have not less than ten (10) years of experience in the insurance or reinsurance industry. No arbitrator shall be a current employee, director, or officer of either Party or of any affiliate of either Party. The umpire shall be impartial and independent of both Parties.

**15.7 Honorable Engagement.** The arbitrators shall interpret this Treaty as an honorable engagement between the Parties and not merely as a legal obligation. With due consideration to the customs and practices of the insurance and reinsurance industry, the arbitrators shall make their award with a view to effecting the general purpose of this Treaty in a reasonable manner, rather than in accordance with a literal interpretation of its language. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the arbitrators shall not have the power to abrogate or modify any express provision of this Treaty.

**15.8 Fee-Shifting.** The losing Party, as determined by the arbitration panel, shall pay the prevailing Party\'s reasonable attorneys\' fees and legal costs, together with all costs and expenses of the arbitration, including the fees and expenses of the arbitrators and the umpire, the costs of any hearing facilities, and any administrative costs. If the arbitration panel determines that neither Party is clearly the prevailing Party, the panel may allocate costs and fees between the Parties as the panel deems equitable.

**15.9 Discovery.** The arbitration panel shall have the authority to order such discovery as it deems necessary and appropriate, including document production, written interrogatories, and depositions. The panel shall have regard to the need for efficiency and proportionality in determining the scope of any discovery ordered.

**15.10 Award.** The award of the arbitration panel shall be in writing and shall state the reasons for the decision. The award shall be final and binding upon the Parties and may be confirmed, recognized, and enforced as a judgment in any court of competent jurisdiction, including courts in the United States under the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (the \"New York Convention\"). The Parties waive any right to appeal the merits of the award to the extent permitted by applicable law.

**15.11 Confidentiality of Proceedings.** All arbitration proceedings conducted under this Article XV, including any hearings, documents, and the final award, shall be confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party except as may be required by law, regulation, or court order, or as necessary for the enforcement of the award.

**15.12 Tolling.** The commencement of arbitration proceedings shall toll any applicable statute of limitations or prescriptive period for the duration of such proceedings.

**[ARTICLE XVI --- INTERMEDIARY]{.underline}**

**16.1 Designated Intermediary.** Baxter & Rowland Intermediaries LLC (\"B&R\"), 150 North Michigan Avenue, Suite 1200, Chicago, Illinois 60601, is hereby recognized as the intermediary through whom all notices, communications, accounts, and payments in connection with this Treaty shall be transmitted, unless otherwise specifically provided herein or agreed in writing by the Parties.

**16.2 Payments by Reinsurer to Intermediary.** Payments made by the Reinsurer to B&R in connection with this Treaty shall be deemed to constitute payment to the Company. The Company shall not have a claim against the Reinsurer for any payment that has been made by the Reinsurer to B&R in accordance with the terms of this Treaty. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Company shall have the right to proceed directly against the Reinsurer for the recovery of any such payment if not received by the Company from B&R within thirty (30) days of the date the Reinsurer made such payment to B&R.

**16.3 Payments by Company to Intermediary.** Payments made by the Company to B&R in connection with this Treaty shall not be deemed to constitute payment to the Reinsurer until such payments are actually received by the Reinsurer. The Company\'s obligation to remit amounts due to the Reinsurer under this Treaty shall not be discharged by payment to B&R unless and until such payments are actually received by the Reinsurer. If B&R fails to transmit to the Reinsurer any payment made by the Company to B&R in connection with this Treaty, the Company shall remain liable to the Reinsurer for such payment, subject to the Company\'s rights and remedies against B&R.

**16.4 Intermediary Not a Party.** B&R is not a party to this Treaty and shall have no rights or obligations hereunder, except as expressly provided in this Article XVI. B&R\'s role is limited to that of an intermediary facilitating communications and payments between the Parties.

**[ARTICLE XVII --- COMMUTATION]{.underline}**

**17.1 Right to Commute.** Either Party may elect to commute this Treaty at any time on or after the third anniversary of the Expiration Date (i.e., on or after January 1, 2029), by giving not less than ninety (90) days\' prior written notice to the other Party (the \"Commutation Notice\"). The Commutation Notice shall specify the proposed commutation date (the \"Commutation Date\"), which shall be not earlier than ninety (90) days following delivery of the Commutation Notice.

**17.2 Determination of Commutation Amount.** The commutation amount (the \"Commutation Amount\") shall be determined by mutual agreement of the Parties, taking into account all outstanding obligations of the Reinsurer under this Treaty, including paid and outstanding Ceded Losses, reserves for known claims, and any other relevant factors. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to agree upon the Commutation Amount within sixty (60) days of the date of the Commutation Notice (the \"Negotiation Period\").

**17.3 Independent Actuary.** If the Parties are unable to agree on the Commutation Amount within the Negotiation Period, the Commutation Amount shall be determined by an independent actuary appointed by mutual agreement of the Parties. If the Parties are unable to agree on the appointment of an independent actuary within thirty (30) days following the expiration of the Negotiation Period, each Party shall appoint one (1) independent actuary, and the two appointed actuaries shall select a third independent actuary who shall serve as the sole determining actuary (the \"Determining Actuary\"). Each Party shall cooperate with the Determining Actuary and provide such data, records, and information as the Determining Actuary may reasonably request.

**17.4 Determination Final and Binding.** The determination of the Commutation Amount by the Determining Actuary shall be final and binding upon the Parties.

**17.5 Discharge.** Upon payment of the Commutation Amount by the Reinsurer to the Company (or by the Company to the Reinsurer, if the Commutation Amount reflects a net balance due to the Reinsurer), the Reinsurer shall be fully and finally discharged from all past, present, and future obligations under this Treaty, and the Company shall release the Reinsurer from all claims arising under or in connection with this Treaty.

**17.6 Trust Release.** Upon payment of the Commutation Amount in full, the Company shall take all actions reasonably necessary to release and discharge the Trust Agreement and to release the trust assets to the Reinsurer, in accordance with the terms of the Trust Agreement.

**[ARTICLE XVIII --- TRUST AGREEMENT]{.underline}**

**18.1 Establishment of Trust.** The Reinsurer has established and shall maintain a trust fund (the \"Trust Fund\") pursuant to the Trust Agreement, dated as of January 1, 2025, among the Company (as beneficiary), the Reinsurer (as grantor), and First Continental Trust Company, N.A. (as trustee) (the \"Trustee\"). The Trust Agreement is incorporated herein by reference and is subject to its own terms and conditions.

**18.2 Purpose.** The Trust Fund is established for the sole benefit of the Company and is intended to collateralize the Reinsurer\'s obligations under this Treaty, including the Reinsurer\'s obligations with respect to Ceded Losses, ALAE, return premiums, and any other amounts due from the Reinsurer to the Company hereunder. The Trust Fund is further intended to enable the Company to obtain full credit for reinsurance ceded under this Treaty in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.

**18.3 Minimum Trust Fund Amount.** The Trust Fund shall be maintained in an amount of not less than Forty-Three Million Dollars (\$43,000,000) at all times (the \"Minimum Trust Fund Amount\"). The Trust Fund shall be invested in assets meeting the requirements of the Trust Agreement, which shall include only United States Treasury securities, obligations of United States government agencies, and investment-grade corporate bonds rated \"A-\" or better by a nationally recognized statistical rating organization (as defined in the Trust Agreement).

**18.4 Annual Adjustment.** The Minimum Trust Fund Amount shall be subject to annual adjustment based on the Reinsurer\'s outstanding obligations under this Treaty, including reserves for known claims, reserves for incurred but not reported claims, and unearned premium reserves. The annual adjustment shall be conducted in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Trust Agreement. In no event shall the Trust Fund be reduced below the Minimum Trust Fund Amount of Forty-Three Million Dollars (\$43,000,000) without the prior written consent of the Company and any applicable regulatory authority.

**18.5 Maintenance.** The Reinsurer shall maintain the Trust Fund in accordance with the terms of the Trust Agreement throughout the term of this Treaty and during the run-off period following the Expiration Date, until all obligations of the Reinsurer hereunder are fully discharged or this Treaty is commuted pursuant to Article XVII.

**18.6 Cross-Reference.** The terms and conditions of the Trust Agreement, including the rights and obligations of the Company, the Reinsurer, and the Trustee with respect to the Trust Fund, are set forth in a separate Trust Agreement document, which is executed contemporaneously with this Treaty.

**[ARTICLE XIX --- TAXES]{.underline}**

**19.1 Responsibility for Taxes.** Each Party shall be solely responsible for its own tax obligations arising under applicable law in connection with this Treaty. Neither Party shall have any obligation to indemnify or reimburse the other Party for any taxes imposed upon such other Party.

**19.2 Federal Excise Tax.** The Company shall be responsible for payment of any federal excise tax applicable to premiums ceded under this Treaty to the extent required under Section 4371 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or any successor provision. The Company shall have no right to recover such excise tax from the Reinsurer, and the Reinsurer shall have no obligation to pay, reimburse, or indemnify the Company for any such excise tax. The Company shall timely file all required returns and pay all excise taxes due in connection with this Treaty.

**19.3 Cooperation.** The Reinsurer shall cooperate with the Company in completing and filing any required tax reporting forms in connection with this Treaty, including without limitation IRS Form 720 (Quarterly Federal Excise Tax Return), IRS Form 5471, or any other applicable United States or Bermuda tax reporting forms. Each Party shall provide to the other Party such information and documentation as may be reasonably required for tax reporting purposes.

**19.4 Withholding.** If either Party is required by applicable law to withhold or deduct any tax from payments due under this Treaty, such Party shall withhold or deduct the required amount and remit it to the appropriate taxing authority. The amount of the payment due to the other Party shall be reduced by the amount withheld or deducted. The withholding Party shall provide the other Party with evidence of such withholding or deduction.

**[ARTICLE XX --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**20.1 Confidential Information.** Each Party agrees that all non-public information received from the other Party in connection with this Treaty, including without limitation financial information, underwriting data, claims data, pricing information, actuarial analyses, policyholder information, and the terms and conditions of this Treaty (collectively, \"Confidential Information\"), shall be treated as confidential and shall not be disclosed to any third party except as provided in this Article XX.

**20.2 Exceptions.** The obligations of confidentiality set forth in Section 20.1 shall not apply to information that:

> \(a\) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of the receiving Party;
>
> \(b\) was already known to the receiving Party at the time of disclosure, as evidenced by the receiving Party\'s written records;
>
> \(c\) is independently developed by the receiving Party without use of or reference to the disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information; or
>
> \(d\) is received by the receiving Party from a third party that is not bound by any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information.

**20.3 Permitted Disclosures.** Notwithstanding Section 20.1, each Party may disclose Confidential Information:

> \(a\) as required by law, regulation, subpoena, or order of a court or governmental or regulatory authority having competent jurisdiction, provided that the disclosing Party shall, to the extent permitted by law, provide the other Party with prompt written notice of such requirement so that the other Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy;
>
> \(b\) to the Party\'s respective auditors, actuaries, legal counsel, reinsurance intermediaries, and retrocessionaires, in each case on a need-to-know basis and subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations;
>
> \(c\) to regulatory authorities having jurisdiction over either Party or its affiliates; and
>
> \(d\) with the prior written consent of the other Party.

**20.4 Survival.** The obligations of confidentiality set forth in this Article XX shall survive the expiration, termination, or commutation of this Treaty for a period of five (5) years.

**[ARTICLE XXI --- NOTICES]{.underline}**

**21.1 Form of Notices.** All notices, requests, demands, consents, approvals, and other communications required or permitted under this Treaty shall be in writing and shall be delivered by hand, by nationally recognized overnight courier service, or by electronic mail (with confirmation of receipt requested), addressed to the applicable Party at the address set forth below, or to such other address as either Party may designate in writing from time to time.

**21.3 Effectiveness.** Notices shall be deemed given and effective: (a) upon delivery, if delivered by hand; (b) on the next business day following deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier service; or (c) upon confirmed receipt, if sent by electronic mail. All notices required or permitted to be given through the Intermediary shall be transmitted through B&R in accordance with Article XVI, unless otherwise expressly provided in this Treaty or agreed in writing by the Parties.

**[ARTICLE XXII --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**22.1 Entire Agreement.** This Treaty, together with the Trust Agreement, the Schedules attached hereto, and any endorsements, addenda, or written amendments hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, understandings, and agreements between the Parties, whether written or oral, relating to such subject matter. No extrinsic evidence, course of dealing, or trade usage shall be used to contradict, modify, or supplement the terms of this Treaty.

**22.2 Amendment.** No amendment, modification, supplement, or waiver of any provision of this Treaty shall be effective unless set forth in a written instrument signed by duly authorized representatives of both Parties. No oral agreement or understanding shall constitute an amendment or modification of this Treaty.

**22.3 Waiver.** No waiver by either Party of any provision of this Treaty, or of any breach thereof, shall constitute a waiver of any other provision or of any subsequent breach of the same or any other provision. No waiver shall be effective unless set forth in a writing signed by the waiving Party. The failure of either Party to enforce any provision of this Treaty shall not be construed as a waiver of such provision or the right to enforce it at a later time.

**22.4 Assignment.** Neither Party may assign, transfer, or delegate any of its rights, interests, or obligations under this Treaty without the prior written consent of the other Party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided, however, that either Party may assign its rights and obligations under this Treaty without the other Party\'s consent in connection with a statutory merger, consolidation, or assumption reinsurance transaction in which the assigning Party\'s obligations under this Treaty are assumed by the surviving or successor entity by operation of law or pursuant to a regulatory-approved assumption agreement.

**22.5 Severability.** If any provision of this Treaty is held by a court of competent jurisdiction or arbitration panel to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable under applicable law, such provision shall be deemed modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal, and enforceable, and the remaining provisions of this Treaty shall continue in full force and effect. If such modification is not possible, the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision shall be deemed severed from this Treaty, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

**22.6 Counterparts.** This Treaty may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution of this Treaty by facsimile signature or electronic signature (including PDF) shall be deemed equivalent to execution by original signature.

**22.7 Headings.** The article and section headings contained in this Treaty are for convenience of reference only and shall not affect the meaning, interpretation, or construction of any provision of this Treaty.

**22.8 Currency.** All monetary amounts referenced in this Treaty, including all premiums, losses, commissions, limits, and other financial terms, are denominated in and shall be paid in United States Dollars.

**22.9 No Third-Party Beneficiaries.** Nothing in this Treaty, express or implied, is intended to confer upon any person or entity other than the Parties (and their permitted successors and assigns) any rights, remedies, obligations, or liabilities under or by reason of this Treaty. The Intermediary is not a third-party beneficiary of this Treaty.

**22.10 Relationship of Parties.** The relationship between the Company and the Reinsurer under this Treaty is that of cedant and reinsurer. Nothing in this Treaty shall be construed to create a partnership, joint venture, agency, or employment relationship between the Parties. Neither Party shall have any authority to bind or obligate the other Party, except as expressly provided herein.

**[ARTICLE XXIII --- EXECUTION]{.underline}**

**23.1 Execution.** IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the Parties hereto have caused this Quota Share Reinsurance Treaty to be executed by their respective duly authorized representatives as of the date first written above.

**[SCHEDULE A]{.underline}**

**[BUSINESS COVERED]{.underline}**

**A.1 Classes of Business.** The following classes of commercial general liability insurance constitute \"Subject Business\" under this Treaty:

> \(a\) **Commercial General Liability (CGL) --- Occurrence Form.** CGL policies written on an occurrence-basis form, including the Company\'s proprietary policy forms and ISO standard forms (CG 00 01 and successor editions), providing coverage for:
>
> \(i\) Premises and operations liability;
>
> \(ii\) Products liability and completed operations liability;
>
> \(iii\) Contractual liability (insured contracts);
>
> \(iv\) Personal injury and advertising injury liability;
>
> \(v\) Medical payments coverage; and
>
> \(vi\) Supplementary payments and related coverages provided as part of the CGL policy.
>
> \(b\) **Commercial General Liability (CGL) --- Claims-Made Form.** CGL policies written on a claims-made basis, including the Company\'s proprietary policy forms and ISO standard forms (CG 00 02 and successor editions), providing the same coverages as set forth in subsection (a) above, subject to the applicable retroactive date and extended reporting period provisions.
>
> \(c\) **Umbrella and Excess Coverage.** Subject Business does NOT include commercial umbrella or excess liability policies. Only primary CGL policies are included.

**A.2 Territory.** Subject Business is limited to policies covering risks located within:

> \(a\) The United States of America, including all fifty (50) states, the District of Columbia, and all territories and possessions of the United States (including Puerto Rico, the U.S. Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, and the Northern Mariana Islands); and
>
> \(b\) Canada, including all provinces and territories.

**A.3 Per-Occurrence Policy Limit Cap.** Subject Business is limited to policies with per-occurrence limits of liability not exceeding Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000), as set forth in Article III, Section 3.3.

**A.4 Exclusions.** The exclusions from Subject Business set forth in Article III, Section 3.4, are incorporated herein by reference and apply in full to this Schedule A.

**A.5 Estimated Premiums.** Based on the Company\'s projections as of December 2024:

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Item**                                                   **Amount**
  ---------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Estimated Net Written Premium (CGL) --- 2025 Treaty Year   \$193,000,000

  Quota Share Percentage                                     30%

  Estimated Ceded Premiums                                   \$57,900,000
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The foregoing estimates are provided for informational purposes only and do not constitute a warranty or guarantee of actual premiums. Actual Ceded Premiums may be higher or lower than the estimated amount based on the Company\'s actual production during the Treaty Year.

**[SCHEDULE B]{.underline}**

**[SLIDING SCALE CEDING COMMISSION TABLE]{.underline}**

**B.1 Sliding Scale Table.** The ceding commission payable by the Reinsurer to the Company under Article VII shall be determined by reference to the following sliding scale, based on the Treaty Year Loss Ratio:

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Treaty Year Loss Ratio**   **Ceding Commission Rate**   **Formula / Basis**
  ---------------------------- ---------------------------- -----------------------------------
  55.00% or below              38.00% (Maximum)             Fixed at maximum rate

  55.01% --- 65.00%            38.00% to 34.00%             38.00% − \[(LR − 55.00%) × 0.40\]

  65.01% --- 75.00%            34.00% to 28.00%             34.00% − \[(LR − 65.00%) × 0.60\]

  Above 75.00%                 28.00% (Minimum)             Fixed at minimum rate
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**B.2 Provisional Rate.** The Provisional Ceding Commission rate is 34.00%, corresponding to an assumed Treaty Year Loss Ratio of 65.00%.

**B.3 Interpolation.** The sliding scale shall be applied on a continuous, straight-line basis within each band. Fractional percentages shall be calculated to two (2) decimal places.

**B.4 Illustrative Examples.** The following examples illustrate the application of the sliding scale at various Loss Ratios:

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Loss Ratio**    **Band**            **Ceding Commission Calculation**                        **Commission Rate**
  ----------------- ------------------- -------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------
  50.00%            ≤ 55.00%            Fixed maximum                                            38.00%

  55.00%            ≤ 55.00%            Fixed maximum                                            38.00%

  58.50%            55.01% --- 65.00%   38.00% − \[(58.50% − 55.00%) × 0.40\] = 38.00% − 1.40%   36.60%

  62.30%            55.01% --- 65.00%   38.00% − \[(62.30% − 55.00%) × 0.40\] = 38.00% − 2.92%   35.08%

  65.00%            55.01% --- 65.00%   38.00% − \[(65.00% − 55.00%) × 0.40\] = 38.00% − 4.00%   34.00%

  68.00%            65.01% --- 75.00%   34.00% − \[(68.00% − 65.00%) × 0.60\] = 34.00% − 1.80%   32.20%

  72.50%            65.01% --- 75.00%   34.00% − \[(72.50% − 65.00%) × 0.60\] = 34.00% − 4.50%   29.50%

  75.00%            65.01% --- 75.00%   34.00% − \[(75.00% − 65.00%) × 0.60\] = 34.00% − 6.00%   28.00%

  80.00%            \> 75.00%           Fixed minimum                                            28.00%

  100.00%           \> 75.00%           Fixed minimum                                            28.00%

  146.80%           \> 75.00%           Fixed minimum                                            28.00%
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**B.5 Adjustment Timing.** The sliding scale adjustment shall be calculated and settled in accordance with the provisions of Article VII, Sections 7.3 and 7.4.

**[SCHEDULE C]{.underline}**

**[PROFIT COMMISSION CALCULATION]{.underline}**

**C.1 Formula.** The Net Treaty Profit and Profit Commission for the Treaty Year shall be calculated as follows:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Line**                **Item**                                **Amount / Formula**
  ----------------------- --------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------
  \(A\)                   Ceded Premiums                          Actual Ceded Premiums for Treaty Year

  \(B\)                   Less: Ceded Losses (including ALAE)     Actual Ceded Losses (incl. ALAE) for Treaty Year

  \(C\)                   Less: Ceding Commission (as adjusted)   Adjusted Ceding Commission per sliding scale

  \(D\)                   Less: Overhead/Margin Allowance         5% × Line (A)

  \(E\)                   Net Treaty Profit                       \(A\) − (B) − (C) − (D), if positive

  \(F\)                   Less: Deficit Carryforward (if any)     From prior period(s), maximum 2-year carryforward

  \(G\)                   Adjusted Net Treaty Profit              \(E\) − (F), if positive

  \(H\)                   Profit Commission (15%)                 15% × Line (G)
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**C.2 Deficit Carryforward.** If the calculation at Line (E) results in a negative number (a \"Deficit\") in any annual recalculation period, such Deficit shall carry forward and must be recovered before any Profit Commission becomes payable. Deficits shall carry forward for a maximum of two (2) consecutive annual recalculation periods, after which any remaining Deficit shall extinguish.

**C.3 Illustrative Example.** The following illustrative example is based on a projected Treaty Year Loss Ratio of 62.30% and estimated Ceded Premiums of \$57,900,000. This example is for illustration purposes only and does not constitute a warranty or guarantee of actual results.

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Line**                **Item**                                                                      **Amount**
  ----------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------
  \(A\)                   Ceded Premiums                                                                \$57,900,000

  \(B\)                   Ceded Losses (including ALAE) at 62.30% LR                                    \$36,082,000

  \(C\)                   Ceding Commission at 35.08% (per Schedule B)                                  \$20,311,000

  \(D\)                   Overhead/Margin Allowance (5% × \$57,900,000)                                 \$2,895,000

  \(E\)                   Net Treaty Profit: \$57,900,000 − \$36,082,000 − \$20,311,000 − \$2,895,000   (\$1,388,000) (Deficit)

  \(F\)                   Deficit Carryforward (from prior periods)                                     \$0

  \(G\)                   Adjusted Net Treaty Profit                                                    (\$1,388,000) (Deficit --- carried forward)

  \(H\)                   Profit Commission                                                             \$0
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In this illustrative scenario, the Net Treaty Profit calculation results in a Deficit of (\$1,388,000), and no Profit Commission would be payable. The Deficit of (\$1,388,000) would carry forward to the next annual recalculation period.

**C.4 Alternative Scenario --- Lower Loss Ratio.** If the Treaty Year Loss Ratio were 55.00% (the maximum commission threshold), the calculation would be as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Line**                **Item**                                                                      **Amount**
  ----------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------
  \(A\)                   Ceded Premiums                                                                \$57,900,000

  \(B\)                   Ceded Losses (including ALAE) at 55.00% LR                                    \$31,845,000

  \(C\)                   Ceding Commission at 38.00% (maximum)                                         \$22,002,000

  \(D\)                   Overhead/Margin Allowance (5% × \$57,900,000)                                 \$2,895,000

  \(E\)                   Net Treaty Profit: \$57,900,000 − \$31,845,000 − \$22,002,000 − \$2,895,000   \$1,158,000

  \(F\)                   Deficit Carryforward                                                          \$0

  \(G\)                   Adjusted Net Treaty Profit                                                    \$1,158,000

  \(H\)                   Profit Commission (15% × \$1,158,000)                                         \$173,700
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**C.5 Timing.** The initial Profit Commission calculation shall be made twenty-four (24) months after the Expiration Date (i.e., as of December 31, 2027), with annual recalculations thereafter, in accordance with Article VIII, Section 8.4.

**[SCHEDULE D]{.underline}**

**[CLAIMS REPORTING THRESHOLDS]{.underline}**

**D.1 Summary of Claims Reporting and Authority Thresholds.** The following table summarizes the claims reporting, consent, and association thresholds applicable under Article XI:

  **Threshold (Incurred Losses --- Gross Basis)**   **Reinsurer\'s Share (at 30% QS)**   **Action Required**                                                        **Timing / Trigger**
  ------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------ -------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  ≥ \$250,000                                       \$75,000                             Individual claim notice to Reinsurer                                       Within 60 days of claim reaching threshold

  ≥ \$500,000                                       \$150,000                            Reinsurer\'s prior written consent required for settlement or compromise   Prior to settlement; Reinsurer to respond within \"reasonable time\"

  ≥ \$750,000                                       \$225,000                            Reinsurer\'s right to associate in defense and control of claim            Upon claim reaching threshold; exercised by written notice
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**D.2 Quarterly Bordereau Reporting.** In addition to the individual claim reporting requirements set forth above, the Company shall provide quarterly premium and loss bordereau reports within forty-five (45) days following the end of each calendar quarter, as set forth in Article IX, Section 9.1.

**D.3 Large Loss Notification.** If any individual claim under Subject Business involves a fatality, catastrophic injury (permanent total disability or severe traumatic brain injury), or a single occurrence with aggregate incurred losses from all claimants exceeding One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000), the Company shall provide prompt telephonic notice to the Reinsurer within five (5) business days, followed by written confirmation within thirty (30) days.

**D.4 Monthly Reporting.** After the aggregate Ceded Losses under this Treaty exceed sixty percent (60%) of the Aggregate Limit (i.e., \$51,000,000), the Company shall provide monthly summary reports of Ceded Losses to the Reinsurer, as set forth in Article VI, Section 6.4.

**D.5 Forms and Format.** The Company and the Reinsurer shall agree upon the format and content of all bordereau and reporting forms prior to the first reporting period. Until such agreement is reached, the Company shall use its standard reporting formats, provided that such formats contain the information required under Articles IX and XI of this Treaty.

**REINSURANCE TRUST AGREEMENT**

This REINSURANCE TRUST AGREEMENT (this \"Agreement\") is made and entered into as of January 10, 2025, by and among:

> \(1\) **ARGONAUT RE LTD.**, a Bermuda-domiciled Class 3B reinsurer with its principal office at Victoria Place, 3rd Floor, 31 Victoria Street, Hamilton HM 10, Bermuda (the \"Grantor\");
>
> \(2\) **PINNACLE CASUALTY INSURANCE COMPANY**, an Illinois domestic stock insurance company (NAIC Company Code 24817) with its principal office at 200 North LaSalle Street, Suite 2800, Chicago, IL 60601 (the \"Beneficiary\"); and
>
> \(3\) **FIRST CONTINENTAL TRUST COMPANY, N.A.**, a national trust company chartered under the laws of the United States, with offices at 388 Greenwich Street, 18th Floor, New York, NY 10013 (the \"Trustee\").

The Grantor, the Beneficiary, and the Trustee are sometimes referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, the Grantor, Argonaut Re Ltd., is a Class 3B reinsurer organized and existing under the laws of Bermuda and registered with the Bermuda Monetary Authority under the Insurance Act 1978, as amended, and has its principal office at Victoria Place, 3rd Floor, 31 Victoria Street, Hamilton HM 10, Bermuda; and

**WHEREAS**, the Beneficiary, Pinnacle Casualty Insurance Company, is a domestic stock insurance company organized and existing under the laws of the State of Illinois, holding NAIC Company Code 24817, and has its principal office at 200 North LaSalle Street, Suite 2800, Chicago, IL 60601; and

**WHEREAS**, the Grantor and the Beneficiary have entered into or propose to enter into that certain Quota Share Reinsurance Treaty effective as of January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2025 (the \"Reinsurance Agreement\"), under which the Grantor has agreed to reinsure thirty percent (30%) of the Beneficiary\'s net retained commercial general liability premiums and losses on terms and subject to the conditions more particularly set forth in the Reinsurance Agreement; and

**WHEREAS**, the Grantor is not licensed, accredited, or certified as a reinsurer in any state or territory of the United States, including the State of Illinois, which is the domiciliary state of the Beneficiary; and

**WHEREAS**, the Beneficiary desires to obtain credit for reinsurance ceded to the Grantor on its statutory financial statements filed with the Illinois Department of Insurance in accordance with applicable law, and the applicable provisions of the Illinois Insurance Code and the regulations promulgated thereunder require the collateralization of the Grantor\'s obligations to the Beneficiary in order for the Beneficiary to take such credit for reinsurance; and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties desire to establish a trust account for the sole benefit of the Beneficiary, to be held and administered by the Trustee, to secure the Grantor\'s obligations to the Beneficiary arising under the Reinsurance Agreement and to facilitate the Beneficiary\'s eligibility for credit for reinsurance ceded to the Grantor; and

**WHEREAS**, First Continental Trust Company, N.A., a national trust company chartered under the laws of the United States, with trust assets under management in excess of Twelve Billion Dollars (\$12,000,000,000), has agreed to serve as Trustee of the trust account established hereunder on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth herein;

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties hereby agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below. Unless the context otherwise requires, capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Reinsurance Agreement.

**Section 1.01.** \"**Beneficiary**\" means Pinnacle Casualty Insurance Company, an Illinois domestic stock insurance company (NAIC Company Code 24817), including any successor to Pinnacle Casualty Insurance Company by operation of law, merger, or consolidation.

**Section 1.02.** \"**Business Day**\" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or a day on which banking institutions in New York, New York, Chicago, Illinois, or Hamilton, Bermuda are authorized or obligated by law or executive order to close.

**Section 1.03.** \"**Eligible Trust Assets**\" means assets of the following types that are deposited in or credited to the Trust Account:

> \(a\) cash in United States dollars;
>
> \(b\) direct obligations of, or obligations the principal and interest of which are unconditionally guaranteed by, the United States of America, including United States Treasury bills, notes, and bonds;
>
> \(c\) investment-grade corporate bonds, notes, or debentures having a credit rating of not less than A- (or its equivalent) by at least one nationally recognized statistical rating organization (as defined by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission), with a remaining maturity not exceeding five (5) years from the date of deposit; and
>
> \(d\) any other assets approved in advance in writing by both the Beneficiary and the applicable insurance regulatory authority having jurisdiction over the Beneficiary.

For the avoidance of doubt, mortgage-backed securities, asset-backed securities, equity securities, mutual fund shares, and derivative instruments shall not constitute Eligible Trust Assets unless specifically approved in writing pursuant to clause (d) above.

**Section 1.04.** \"**Grantor**\" means Argonaut Re Ltd., a Bermuda-domiciled Class 3B reinsurer registered with the Bermuda Monetary Authority.

**Section 1.05.** \"**Illinois Department of Insurance**\" means the Department of Insurance of the State of Illinois, or any successor governmental agency or authority charged with the regulation of insurance in the State of Illinois.

**Section 1.06.** \"**Investment Income**\" means all interest, dividends, coupon payments, and realized capital gains earned or accrued on the Eligible Trust Assets held in the Trust Account, net of any investment-related fees or charges.

**Section 1.07.** \"**Matured Assets**\" means any Eligible Trust Assets held in the Trust Account that have matured or been called for redemption, and the principal proceeds thereof.

**Section 1.08.** \"**Minimum Trust Amount**\" means Forty-Three Million Dollars (\$43,000,000).

**Section 1.09.** \"**NAIC**\" means the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, or any successor organization thereto.

**Section 1.10.** \"**Offset Rights**\" means the right of either the Grantor or the Beneficiary to offset any balance or amount owed by one party to the other under the Reinsurance Agreement against any balance or amount owed by the other party under any other reinsurance agreement between the Grantor and the Beneficiary, as more particularly described in Article VIII of the Reinsurance Agreement.

**Section 1.11.** \"**Person**\" means any individual, corporation, partnership, limited liability company, trust, governmental entity, or other legal entity.

**Section 1.12.** \"**Prior Written Notice**\" means written notice delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 11.03 of this Agreement not fewer than five (5) Business Days prior to the action to which such notice relates, unless a different notice period is specified in this Agreement.

**Section 1.13.** \"**Reinsurance Agreement**\" means that certain Quota Share Reinsurance Treaty between the Grantor and the Beneficiary effective as of January 1, 2025, through December 31, 2025, as the same may be amended, modified, supplemented, extended, or renewed from time to time by written agreement of the parties thereto.

**Section 1.14.** \"**Reinsurance Obligations**\" means all obligations of the Grantor to the Beneficiary arising under or in connection with the Reinsurance Agreement, including without limitation the Grantor\'s share of ceded losses, ceded allocated loss adjustment expenses (\"ALAE\"), and the return of unearned premiums, in each case as determined in accordance with the terms of the Reinsurance Agreement, subject to the Aggregate Limit (as defined in the Reinsurance Agreement) and any applicable Offset Rights under Article VIII of the Reinsurance Agreement.

**Section 1.15.** \"**Required Trust Amount**\" means Forty-Three Million Dollars (\$43,000,000), as such amount may be adjusted from time to time pursuant to Section 4.02 of this Agreement; *provided, however*, that the Required Trust Amount shall not at any time fall below the Minimum Trust Amount of Forty-Three Million Dollars (\$43,000,000).

**Section 1.16.** \"**Trust Account**\" or \"**Trust Fund**\" means the trust account established and maintained by the Trustee pursuant to this Agreement for the sole benefit of the Beneficiary, to be known as the \"Argonaut Re Ltd. --- Pinnacle Casualty Insurance Company Reinsurance Trust,\" including all Eligible Trust Assets deposited therein, all Investment Income earned thereon, and all proceeds thereof.

**Section 1.17.** \"**Trustee**\" means First Continental Trust Company, N.A., a national trust company, and any successor trustee appointed pursuant to Section 6.05 of this Agreement.

**Section 1.18.** \"**Withdrawal Notice**\" means a written notice in substantially the form set forth in Exhibit A hereto, delivered by the Beneficiary to the Trustee, requesting the withdrawal of assets from the Trust Account.

**[ARTICLE II --- ESTABLISHMENT OF TRUST ACCOUNT]{.underline}**

**Section 2.01 --- Creation of Trust**

The Grantor hereby establishes and creates a trust account with the Trustee, to be known as the \"Argonaut Re Ltd. --- Pinnacle Casualty Insurance Company Reinsurance Trust\" (the \"Trust Account\"), for the sole benefit of the Beneficiary. The Trust Account shall be established and maintained by the Trustee at its offices located at 388 Greenwich Street, 18th Floor, New York, NY 10013, or at such other location as the Trustee may designate from time to time with prior written notice to the Grantor and the Beneficiary. The Trust Account shall be a separate and distinct account, segregated from all other assets of the Grantor, the Trustee, and any other person. The Trustee shall hold legal title to all assets in the Trust Account for the benefit of the Beneficiary, subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement. The Grantor retains equitable ownership of the assets deposited in the Trust Account, subject in all respects to the Beneficiary\'s prior right to withdraw assets therefrom in accordance with Article V.

**Section 2.02 --- Purpose**

The Trust Account is established for the sole purpose of securing the Grantor\'s Reinsurance Obligations to the Beneficiary under the Reinsurance Agreement, and to permit the Beneficiary to obtain credit for reinsurance ceded to the Grantor on the Beneficiary\'s statutory financial statements filed with the Illinois Department of Insurance. The assets held in the Trust Account shall be available only for the purposes set forth in this Agreement and, in particular, shall be available to satisfy the Grantor\'s Reinsurance Obligations to the Beneficiary. The Trust Account is intended to comply with the applicable provisions of the Illinois Insurance Code (215 ILCS 5/) and the regulations promulgated thereunder by the Illinois Department of Insurance relating to credit for reinsurance ceded to unauthorized reinsurers. The Parties acknowledge that the Grantor is not licensed, accredited, or certified as a reinsurer in the State of Illinois and that the Trust Account serves as collateral to support the Beneficiary\'s entitlement to credit for reinsurance on its statutory financial statements.

**Section 2.03 --- Irrevocability**

The Trust Account established pursuant to this Agreement is irrevocable. The Grantor shall have no right or power to revoke, terminate, or amend this Agreement or to withdraw, transfer, or otherwise remove any assets from the Trust Account except as specifically and expressly provided herein. Any purported revocation, termination, amendment, or withdrawal by the Grantor that is not made in strict compliance with the provisions of this Agreement shall be void and of no force or effect.

**[ARTICLE III --- INITIAL FUNDING]{.underline}**

**Section 3.01 --- Initial Deposit**

Within ten (10) Business Days following the execution of this Agreement by all three Parties, the Grantor shall deposit into the Trust Account Eligible Trust Assets having an aggregate fair market value of not less than Forty-Three Million Dollars (\$43,000,000). The initial funding amount was determined based on the Parties\' good-faith estimate of the Grantor\'s anticipated Reinsurance Obligations during the first year of the Reinsurance Agreement, taking into account the following considerations: (a) the estimated ceded premium under the Reinsurance Agreement of Fifty-Seven Million Nine Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$57,900,000), being thirty percent (30%) of the Beneficiary\'s projected 2025 commercial general liability net written premium of One Hundred Ninety-Three Million Dollars (\$193,000,000); (b) the historical loss experience on the Beneficiary\'s commercial general liability portfolio; and (c) the anticipated timing of premium collections and loss payments. The Grantor shall deliver to the Trustee written instructions for the deposit of the initial Eligible Trust Assets, together with such documentation as the Trustee may reasonably require to confirm the identity, eligibility, and value of such assets. The Trustee shall acknowledge receipt of the initial deposit in writing to both the Grantor and the Beneficiary within two (2) Business Days of the deposit date.

**Section 3.02 --- Composition of Initial Deposit**

The initial deposit of Eligible Trust Assets shall consist of one or more of the following types of assets: (a) United States Treasury securities (including Treasury bills, notes, and bonds); (b) investment-grade corporate bonds, notes, or debentures with a credit rating of not less than A- (or its equivalent) by at least one nationally recognized statistical rating organization, with a remaining maturity not exceeding five (5) years; and (c) cash in United States dollars. Not later than five (5) Business Days prior to the initial deposit, the Grantor shall provide to the Trustee and the Beneficiary a schedule (in substantially the form of Exhibit B hereto) listing the specific assets to be deposited, including for each security: the description of the asset, the CUSIP number (if applicable), the par or face value, the coupon rate or yield, the maturity date, the credit rating and rating agency, and the current fair market value as of the most recent Business Day. The Beneficiary shall have the right, but not the obligation, to review and comment on the proposed composition of the initial deposit prior to its transfer to the Trust Account.

**[ARTICLE IV --- MAINTENANCE AND ADJUSTMENT OF TRUST FUND]{.underline}**

**Section 4.01 --- Maintenance Obligation**

The Grantor shall at all times maintain Eligible Trust Assets in the Trust Account having an aggregate fair market value of not less than the Required Trust Amount. The Trustee shall value the Eligible Trust Assets held in the Trust Account on the last Business Day of each calendar quarter (March 31, June 30, September 30, and December 31) using fair market values as published by a nationally recognized pricing service reasonably selected by the Trustee. In the event that the aggregate fair market value of the Eligible Trust Assets held in the Trust Account falls below the Required Trust Amount as of any such quarterly valuation date, or at any other time as determined by the Trustee or the Beneficiary, the Trustee or the Beneficiary shall promptly deliver written notice to the Grantor specifying the amount of the deficiency.
